name: Image
propertyCopy: Corner radius, aspect ratio and caption are properties of the same component, not separate markup - change them below to check this frame's states in the Live Preview.
guide: Component Guide Human View Machine View Overview Image displays a photo or graphic with graceful loading, error, and hover-preview states built in - a styled wrapper around a real image with defined placeholder, broken-image, and zoom-preview behavior, instead of a bare, unstyled tag with no fallback handling. When to Use A product gallery or article cover photo - any primary visual content that benefits from a defined loading/error state. User-generated content previews - images uploaded by users, which may occasionally fail to load. Document thumbnails or an avatar upload preview - anywhere an image needs consistent framing and fallback handling. When Not to Use A small identity graphic representing a person - use Avatar, which is purpose-built for that role, including initials fallback. A purely decorative background graphic with no meaningful content - a plain CSS background may be simpler than the full Image component's loading/error machinery. An icon - use the system's icon set rather than the Image component for small vector glyphs. Best Practices Always define a visible loading placeholder that matches the image's eventual aspect ratio, so the layout doesn't jump once it loads. Show a clear, distinct broken-image state (not just a blank box) when a URL fails to resolve. Use the hover-zoom/preview behavior only where inspecting detail actually matters (a product photo), not on every image site-wide. Do and Don't Do Warehouse floor plan, Level 2 A caption that says what the image actually is, useful the moment the picture itself fails to load. Don't Image No caption and no alt text means a failed image leaves nothing behind but an empty box - the content is simply gone for that user. Accessibility Every image carries meaningful alt text describing its content, or an empty alt when it's purely decorative. The broken-image fallback state is still announced meaningfully, not left as an unlabeled empty box. Zoom/preview interactions are reachable and dismissible by keyboard, not mouse-hover-only.
